The '''2016 Copa Sudamericana finals''' were scheduled to be the two-legged final that would have decided the winners of the [[2016 Copa Sudamericana]], the 15th edition of the [[Copa Sudamericana]], [[South America]]'s secondary international club [[association football|football]] tournament organized by [[CONMEBOL]].

The finals were scheduled to be contested in two-legged home-and-away format between Colombian team [[Atlético Nacional]] and Brazilian team [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]]. The first leg was scheduled to be hosted by Atlético Nacional at [[Atanasio Girardot Sports Complex|Estadio Atanasio Girardot]] in [[Medellín]] on 30 November 2016, while the second leg was scheduled to be hosted by Chapecoense at [[Estádio Couto Pereira]] in [[Curitiba]] on 7 December 2016. The winner would have earned the right to play against the [[2016 Copa Libertadores]] winners in the [[2017 Recopa Sudamericana]], and against the [[2016 J. League Cup]] winners in the [[2017 Suruga Bank Championship]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/copa_sudamericana_2016_-_reglamento.pdf|title=Copa Sudamericana 2016 – Reglamento|language=es|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref> They also automatically qualified for the [[2017 Copa Libertadores]] group stage.

However, the finals never took place. The matches were cancelled after the crash of [[LaMia Flight 2933]], which was carrying the majority of the [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]] squad on their way to the first leg of the finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-38140981|title=Brazil football team Chapecoense in Colombia plane crash|publisher=BBC|date=29 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Comunicado La Opinion Publica"/> CONMEBOL awarded the title to [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]] on 5 December 2016, following a request by [[Atlético Nacional]].<ref name="Campeón de la Sudamericana 2016"/><ref>[https://www.infobae.com/america/deportes/2016/12/05/la-conmebol-proclamo-al-chapecoense-campeon-de-la-copa-sudamericana-2016/ La Conmebol proclamó al Chapecoense campeón de la Copa Sudamericana 2016] on Infobae, 5 Dec 2016</ref>

Both teams would face each other at the [[2017 Recopa Sudamericana]], since Atlético Nacional won the [[2016 Copa Libertadores|2016 edition]] of the Copa Libertadores, The Recopa title was won by Atlético Nacional.

[[Atlético Nacional]] would have had the chance to complete the [[Copa Libertadores]] and [[Copa Sudamericana]] season double, having won the Copa Libertadores title earlier in [[2016 Copa Libertadores finals|2016]], while this would be the first South American club final for [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]]. Nowadays, that is not possible anymore, given that since 2017, both competitions are played simultaneously.

| footer            = [[Estadio Atanasio Girardot]] in [[Medellín]] (left) and [[Estadio Couto Pereira]] in [[Curitiba]] were scheduled to host the series. Couto Pereira venue was chosen since Chapecoense's stadium, [[Arena Condá]] in [[Chapecó]], did not have the minimum capacity of 40,000 spectators required by CONMEBOL.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/copa-sudamericana-chapecoense-hara-de-local-en-la-final-en-el-estadio-couto-pereira-de-curitiba|title=Copa Sudamericana: Chapecoense hará de local en la final en el estadio "Couto Pereira", de Curitiba|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=25 November 2016}}</ref>
}}
The final would be played on a home-and-away [[two-legged tie|two-legged]] basis, with the higher-seeded team hosting the second leg. If tied on aggregate, the [[away goals rule]] would not be used, and 30 minutes of [[extra time (association football)|extra time]] would be played. If still tied after extra time, the [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] would be used to determine the winner.<ref name="regulations"/>

==LaMia Flight 2933 crash==
{{Main|LaMia Flight 2933}}
On 28 November 2016, LaMia Flight 2933, carrying the [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]] squad to the first leg, crashed on the way to the [[José María Córdova International Airport]].<ref name="Gu live">{{cite news|last1=Weaver|first1=Matthew|last2=Walker|first2=Bonnie|title=Brazilian football team Chapecoense on plane that crashed in Colombia|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2016/nov/29/brazilian-team-chapecoense-onboard-plane-that-crashed-over-colombia-latest|work=The Guardian|date=29 November 2016|access-date=29 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=76 confirmed dead in Colombian plane crash|date=29 November 2016 |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2016/11/29/americas/colombia-plane-accident/index.html|publisher=Cable News Network|access-date=29 November 2016}}</ref> There were 71 fatalities, including 19 of the 22 Chapecoense players on the plane.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-38155840|title=Chapecoense plane crash: The victims, the survivors and those left behind|publisher=BBC|date=1 December 2016}}</ref> CONMEBOL immediately suspended all activities, including the scheduled final matches, in the early morning of 29 November.<ref name="Comunicado La Opinion Publica">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/comunicado-la-opinion-publica|title=Comunicado a la opinión pública|publisher=CONMEBOL|date=29 November 2016|language=es}}</ref>

In light of these events, [[Atlético Nacional]] requested that CONMEBOL award the title to [[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]].<ref name="Campeón de la Sudamericana">{{cite web|title=Campeón de la Sudamericana|url=http://www.atlnacional.com.co/ultimas-noticias/campeon-de-la-sudamericana-015298|publisher=Atlético Nacional de Medellín|access-date=29 November 2016|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170129192510/http://www.atlnacional.com.co/ultimas-noticias/campeon-de-la-sudamericana-015298|archive-date=2017-01-29|url-status=dead}}</ref> As requested, CONMEBOL awarded Chapecoense the title of the 2016 Copa Sudamericana, their first continental title, on 5 December,<ref name="Chape é declarada campeã e garante ao menos US$ 4,8 mi em premiações">{{cite web|title=Chape é declarada campeã e garante ao menos US$ 4,8 mi em premiações|date=5 December 2016 |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/sc/futebol/times/chapecoense/noticia/2016/12/chape-e-declarada-campea-e-garante-ao-menos-us-48-mi-em-premiacoes.html|publisher=globo.com|access-date=5 December 2016|language=pt}}</ref> while Atlético Nacional received the "CONMEBOL Centenario Fair Play" award for their gesture.<ref name="Campeón de la Sudamericana 2016">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/conmebol-otorga-el-titulo-de-campeon-de-la-sudamericana-2016-chapecoense-y-reconoce-atletico |title=CONMEBOL otorga el título de Campeón de la Sudamericana 2016 a Chapecoense y reconoce a Atlético Nacional con el premio del Centenario de la Conmebol al Fair Play |publisher=CONMEBOL.com |date=5 December 2016 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161206042227/http://www.conmebol.com/es/conmebol-otorga-el-titulo-de-campeon-de-la-sudamericana-2016-chapecoense-y-reconoce-atletico |archive-date=6 December 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/dec/05/chapecoense-copa-sudamericana-champions|title=Chapecoense named Copa Sudamericana winners after plane crash|date=5 December 2016|work=Guardian|access-date=5 December 2016}}</ref>

Atlético Nacional invited fans to the [[Atanasio Girardot Sports Complex|Estadio Atanasio Girardot]] dressed in white with candles at the scheduled time of the first leg, to pay tribute in memory to the victims of the crash.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlnacional.com.co/ultimas-noticias/de-luto-015304|archive-url=https://archive.today/20161211082602/http://www.atlnacional.com.co/ultimas-noticias/de-luto-015304|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 11, 2016|title=De Luto|publisher=Atlético Nacional|date=29 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/homenaje-chapecoense-en-medellin|title=Homenaje a Chapecoense en Medellín|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=30 November 2016}}</ref> A vigil was held on the same night at Chapecoense's stadium, the [[Arena Condá]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/y-chapeco-le-canto-su-pena-infinita|title=Y Chapecó le cantó a su pena infinita|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=30 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-38166681|title=Colombia plane crash: Thousands gather for vigils|publisher=BBC|date=1 December 2016}}</ref>
